data.narrative:
Anatar is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Kaia Rhodes. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of seven same-sector peers at Series B and Series D stages, supplemented by reference to a broader set of nine private companies and one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) in robotics and manufacturing infrastructure.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach. The seven identified peers—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D)—yield a median valuation of $1.6B with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. This method directly anchors the analysis given stage-appropriate comparability and sector alignment.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median point estimate of $1.6B. Key uncertainties include the timing and economics of Anatar's deployment relative to peer benchmarks, capital efficiency relative to the Series B cohort, and the durability of current robotics sector multiples. With only one valuation method yielding sufficient data, sensitivity to peer selection and stage-mix assumptions is material. Additional financial metrics on revenue, unit economics, or customer concentration would improve conviction in the range.
